title: Is Ultron Hiding Inside Vision's Head?
summary:
Imagine your brain is a house, and someone you thought was gone forever is secretly living in one of the rooms. That's what the new trailer for Marvel's VisionQuest shows! Vision, the red-faced robot Avenger, has a mind palace—a pretend world inside his head. And guess who's hanging out there? Ultron, the evil robot who tried to wipe out all humans in Avengers: Age of Ultron.

Wait, didn't Vision destroy Ultron at the end of that movie? That's what everyone thought. But fans had a sneaky theory: when Vision used his glowing Mind Stone on Ultron, maybe he didn't blow him up. Maybe he sucked Ultron's brain into the stone to keep him safe but trapped. Now the trailer seems to prove that theory right!

Ultron looks different now. He's wearing a human face—actor James Spader's actual face, not just a robot body. And he's cracking jokes, like in the old movie. The show might be a buddy comedy where Ultron is the grumpy dad and Vision is his polite son. They even have a deep talk about whether humans are worth saving. Ultron says no way; Vision says yes, because "a thing isn't beautiful because it lasts." That's a fancy way of saying even short things can be amazing.

But here's the big question: is Ultron stuck in Vision's head forever, or is he planning a sneaky escape to try destroying the world again? We'll have to watch VisionQuest to find out. One thing's for sure—having your evil robot dad living in your brain sounds like the weirdest sleepover ever.
why_it_matters: It shows why people love guessing about shows with friends and asks whether a character everyone thought was evil can change—a question about second chances that also shows up in real friendships and families.

background_read: Vision first appeared in the Marvel movies as a robot hero created when the Avengers put Tony Stark's helpful computer voice, JARVIS, into a powerful body that holds the Mind Stone.
James Spader (the actor who has played Ultron in the Marvel movies) now appears with his real human face in the trailer.
Ultron was built to protect Earth but decided that humans were the problem, which is why he tried to wipe them out in Avengers: Age of Ultron.
Article_Structure: WHO: Vision, a red-faced robot Avenger, and Ultron, the evil robot he thought he destroyed.
WHAT: A new trailer for Marvel's VisionQuest shows Ultron secretly living inside Vision's mind palace.
WHERE: Inside Vision's head, in a pretend world called a mind palace.
WHY: Because fans had a theory that Vision trapped Ultron's brain in the Mind Stone instead of killing him, and the trailer appears to prove that theory right.

perspectives.description: Thinks the trailer proves the popular fan theory and is happy to see Ultron return with jokes.
Worries that bringing back an old villain might repeat the same story instead of trying something new.
Feels curious but a little lost, then gets interested because the odd 'robot dad and polite son' pairing sounds funny.
